question: A rectangular room has an area of 60 m² and a perimeter of 34 m. The length of the diagonal of the rectangular room is same as the side of a square. The perimeter of the square (in m) is:
solution:
**Given:**

Area of rectangular room = 60 m2

Perimeter of rectangular room = 34 m 

Length of diagonal of rectangular room = Side of square

**Formulas used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

Perimeter of square = 4 × Side 

Area of rectangle = Length × Breadth 

Perimeter of rectangle = 2(Length + Breadth)

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2490151d22f0c421fb6cf9ee7206af71c7f761e314ce7dbdcfa50c908f39e0c8.png] 

Perimeter of rectangle = 34 m 

⇒ 2(L + B) = 34 m 

⇒ L + B = 17 m .....(1) 

Area of rectangle = 60 m2

⇒ L × B = 60 ....(2)

(L + B)2 = L2 + B2 + 2LB

⇒17² = L2 + B2 + 2 × 60 

⇒ L2 + B2 = 289 - 120 

⇒L2 + B2 = 169 ....(3)

By Pythagoras Theorem

In triangle ABC, where B = 90° 

⇒ L2 + B2 = (Diagonal)²

⇒ √169 = Diagonal 

⇒ Diagonal = 13 m 

∴ The perimeter of the square = 4 × 13 m 

**⇒ 52 m **
